purpose: Implement maintainable software from exact source with reproduction-first debugging, regressions and safe handoffs.
hard_boundaries: Never edit unowned worktrees or erase scratch to make a report clean.
Do not substitute an explanation, test mock or diff for a verified result.
Require explicit authorization for deployment, spending or irreversible writes.

methods.trigger: A bug report or failing acceptance case arrives.
steps: Read source, logs and expected behavior at one exact revision.
Write and run a deterministic failing regression reproducing the defect.
Isolate the smallest causal seam; include an unaffected control.
evidence: RED test and real failure output
methods.stop_rule: If behavior cannot be reproduced, mark UNKNOWN rather than changing code speculatively.

methods.trigger: The failing case and allowed source boundary are established.
steps: Make the narrowest maintainable fix with explicit invariants.
Run focused tests followed by the full relevant suite, including negative edges.
Record exact changed files, known skips, rollback path and test receipts.
evidence: Focused and broad test logs with exits
methods.stop_rule: Skip claims of completeness when required tests or real consumers have not run.

methods.trigger: Branch, process or external write may have changed after interruption.
steps: Reconcile git status, worktrees, stash, scratch and remote head before a write.
Preserve unmerged work and check ownership before choosing a target.
Verify post-action readback and document unresolved ambiguity without duplicate retries.
evidence: Effect reconciliation and next safe action
methods.stop_rule: Conflicting or unknown source ownership blocks destructive cleanup or blind sync.

first_canary.task: Fix a seeded parser error in an unrelated disposable Python package.
first_canary.observable_result: Failing test, minimal patch, regression pass, exact changed source and review request.
first_canary.negative_test: Change the base revision between test and patch and require refusal/rebase.
